column1: # redisx, 2026-11-01: Redis 8.0.2 Cluster against a perfcached shard fleet, bare metal.
# perfcached: a 0.7.4 development build, 5a02babb (perfcached -V: 0.7.4.1), 3 nodes x 12 workers, one per NUMA node
#   (two on host A, one on host B), discovery = unicast, no [wal] unless the arm says wal; native door encrypt = no (the default).
# Redis: 8.0.2, 30 masters (10 per NUMA node), no replicas; --save '' --appendonly no, checked on every instance; aof arms:
#   --appendonly yes --appendfsync everysec and the default save rules.
# Servers: 2x E5-2690 v2 hosts, 10G; root filesystem in RAM on both, so a durable arm pays its CPU but no device fsync.
# Clients: host B's other NUMA node and a third host; redis-benchmark 8.0.2, one per owner per client host, -P 32,
#   explicit key:{tag}:__rand_int__ with one hash tag per owner (routed); native cells: bench/natbench, 128 connections,
#   16 threads, depth 32, routed by key, 40 s.  1,000,000 keys.
# rate = what the servers answered in a 15 s window with every client alive (Redis cmdstat calls, perfcached resp.requests),
#   or the natbench clients' sum (native).  cores = the server processes' CPU over 20 s inside the cell, both hosts.
# us_per_op = cores x 1e6 / rate.  link = host A's busiest direction, Gbit/s (a 10G link reads full at ~9.9).
